Hi Jane —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our discovery / validation conversation and recommended next steps for the embeddings pilot: 

1) Goal & success criteria
- Primary goal: improve semantic search relevance for product FAQs and customer conversations (sample size ~50k docs).
- Success metrics: MRR @10, Recall@10 on labeled queries, and a manual top-10 precision check across 100 queries.

2) Recommended models for pilot
- Primary: redwood-embed-sim-1024 (recommended for balanced accuracy/cost)
- Cost-optimized: open-embed-768-quant (lower memory; acceptable for short docs)
- If you need higher recall for long passages: redwood-embed-2048 (higher dimensionality)

3) Key evaluation notes
- We'll run a small eval harness (attached benchmarks) measuring cosine similarity distributions, MRR, and cluster separability (silhouette) across your taxonomy.
- Watch for embedding norm drift and dimensionality sensitivity — longer docs may benefit from 1024+ dims.

4) Data & access we need
- A 1k-doc sample (representative mix) + top 100 user search queries and expected results / gold set.
- Access via a temporary S3 bucket or Drive link.

5) Next steps / timeline
- You: share sample docs and top queries by Thu 24 Mar
- Us: run baseline eval on two model candidates and share results + prompt set tuning by Tue 30 Mar
- Technical deep-dive: propose Tue 30 Mar, 11am PT (30-45m)

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv, semantic_benchmarks_20270321.pdf (see benchmarks summary / baseline).

If this looks right, I’ll spin up the eval runs and loop in Marissa for tuning.

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Fwd: Embeddings fit validation follow-up — model/monitoring recommendations (internal)

Marissa / Neha — forwarding the thread. Key asks from Acme: sample 1k docs, top 100 queries, keep memory footprint in mind (they currently index at 768-d). My suggested plan: 

- Run redwood-embed-sim-1024 and open-embed-768-quant on the sample. Compare MRR@10, Recall@10, and cosine distribution overlap.
- If 1024 gives >8% MRR uplift vs 768, recommend moving indexing to 1024; otherwise favor the quantized 768 for cost savings.
- Monitoring: push three checks into the pilot telemetry — 1) embedding norm distribution (mean/std) drift; 2) cosine similarity shift between historical and new queries (Kolmogorov–Smirnov test); 3) per-query top-10 precision drop. Alert thresholds doc: see Drive folder.

Risks: if docs contain long concatenated transcripts, we may see hubness in low-dim vectors (false positives). Recommend trying document chunking + mean pooling and evaluating dimensionality impact.

I’ve attached the small sample vector file and the prompt set we'll use for relevance scoring. Can you help with the eval harness and the initial prompt tuning?

—Marcus
[Attachment: embedding_sample_vectors.jsonl (JSONL, 420KB)]
[Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_acme-pilot-evals]

Hi Jane / Samir —

Thanks for confirming — that timeline works. Quick answers to your questions: 

- Dimensionality lift: moving from 768 -> 1024 increases index storage ~33% (depends on quantization). We can provide a cost estimate once we run the two model candidates; if you prefer minimal infra changes, we’ll prioritize the quantized 768 variant as a baseline.
- Drift monitoring: implement the three telemetry checks I outlined in the forwarded note (norm distribution, cosine KS test, per-query precision). We can run the initial thresholds during pilot and tune alerts.
- Cost estimate: ballpark for redwood-embed-sim-1024 during eval (inference + storage amortized): ~$0.80 per 1k queries (subject to volume pricing). The quantized 768 variant is typically ~40-60% cheaper. We’ll provide exact numbers in the report.

Next steps:
- Samir: please drop the 1k sample and top-100 queries into the Drive folder by EOD Thu (I created a folder and shared).
- Marcus/Marissa/Neha: we'll run baseline evals and send a results doc + sample prompt-set tuned PR by Tue 30 Mar.

If everything looks good I’ll open a HubSpot deal and attach the evaluation plan.
